title: Sweet & Sour Turkey Burgers
ingredients: ¼ cup red onion, finely diced (⅛ of whole)
method: Add all turkey patty ingredients (except olive oil) to a large bowl and mix well.
Shape into patties — the base recipe makes 6, but Amy typically gets 9 smaller patties.
Pan-fry in olive oil until cooked through and golden brown on both sides.
notes: Take the extra time to dice the red onion and bird's eye chillies as fine as possible — it helps make the texture smoother. Amy's batch size varies between 6–9 patties; macros are based on 9. Per patty (9/batch): ~11g protein, ~0.5g fibre, ~90 calories.

title: Chicken Sausage & Herby Egg Muffins
ingredients: 12 chicken patties (~87g each, from 1kg chicken mince)
method: Preheat oven to 180°C. Whisk eggs, milk, dill, spring onions, lemon zest, and salt together.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper, pour egg mixture in. Bake 15 mins, then cover with foil for 5 more mins if needed until set.
Cool, then slice the egg sheet into 12 equal squares.
Cook chicken patties separately.
Stack each muffin: English muffin → egg square → chicken patty → cheese slice.
Wrap individually in parchment paper. Refrigerate or freeze.
Reheat from fridge: 10 mins at 180°C. From freezer: thaw first, then same.
notes: Renee recommends making double — freeze half, keep the rest in the fridge. Per muffin: ~446 cal, 38g protein, 39g carbs, 15g fat. The chicken patty recipe is linked separately on Renee's Instagram.

title: 5-Ingredient Maple Sage Chicken Sausage Patties
method: Mix the spices (sage, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper) together.
Add spice mix and maple syrup to the chicken mince. Combine well.
Divide into desired patty size — larger for breakfast sausage, smaller for sliders.
Cook in a hot pan for a few minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
notes: Renee created this for the many people who can't or don't eat eggs but still want a prep-ahead breakfast protein. The psyllium husk is optional but adds fibre. The chicken patties can be used in the Herby Egg Muffins recipe (freeze extras). Macros are per patty for an 8-patty batch.

title: Jammy Eggs in Chilli Oil
method: Boil eggs for ~6.5 minutes for jammy yolks.
Transfer to cold water bath for 5 minutes, then peel.
Add peeled eggs to a container, drizzle with tamari, sesame oil, and chilli oil.
Top with chopped spring onions or parsley.
Serve warm over rice. Keeps for days in the fridge.
notes: Dead simple, high-protein snack. Also good on toast with avocado and rocket. For 2 eggs + 1 cup rice: ~20g protein, ~400 kcal.

title: Protein Pancakes
method: Mash banana. Whisk in eggs.
Add all remaining ingredients.
Cook over medium heat with some butter.
Serve with Chobani low-fat yoghurt and berries.
notes: Reneelynch's note: 'These are dense. Maybe split servings into 2, or if you've lifted heavy weights this will hit the spot.' 47g protein for the full batch. Sub Chief Whey for True Protein — similar macros.

title: Sardine & Yoghurt Dip
method: Drain sardines. Mash with a fork in a bowl.
Add Greek yoghurt, lemon juice, capers, red onion, and spring onion.
Mix well. Serve as a spread on toast or dip with cucumber slices.
notes: Stock Merchant sardines recommended (code BOOBTOFOOD). One tin = ~23g protein. With yoghurt, the full batch hits ~30g protein. Great high-protein snack.

title: 4-Ingredient Chocolate Mousse
ingredients: 1 Tbsp gelatin mixed with ½ cup boiling water
method: Mix gelatin with boiling water and stir well to dissolve.
Add all ingredients to a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth.
Pour into small glass jars. Pop in fridge until set.
notes: Protein-rich dessert — no whey needed. 24g protein per batch (~8g per serve). Add vanilla, orange oil, or peppermint for variety. Adjust sweetness to taste.

title: Sausage Rolls
ingredients: Pinch of sea salt and black pepper
Sesame or poppy seeds, for garnish
method: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line two trays with baking paper.
Mix pork, lamb, garlic, zucchini, carrot, coriander, salt, pepper, and half the whisked egg.
Slice each pastry sheet into thirds. Divide mixture into 9 logs, place on pastry strips.
Fold pastry over filling, overlapping slightly. Press to seal, seam side down. Slice each log into 6 pieces.
Brush tops with remaining egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and flaky salt.
Bake 15–20 min, reduce to 180°C fan-forced, bake extra 10–15 min until golden.
Cool on wire rack to keep base crisp.
notes: Makes 18. Freeze well — serve warm or cold. Great lunchbox protein for kids. ~8g protein per roll, 2 rolls = 16g. Serve with homemade tomato sauce.

title: Sweet Potato & PB Brownies
method: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Mix wet ingredients (excluding peanut butter). Add baking powder, baking soda, and chopped chocolate. Mix in coconut flour.
Pour into lined square baking tray. Drizzle with peanut butter, swirl with a knife.
Bake 30 min, check and cook 5 min longer if needed — should look slightly cracked on top.
notes: No pre-cooking the sweet potato — grated raw into the batter. First shared by Renee in 2013. Add collagen for extra protein. Skip PB and add raspberries for lunchbox-friendly. ~3.4g P per brownie (batch of 9).

title: Zucchini Fritters
ingredients: 4 Tbsp finely chopped dill or chives
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges
2 Tbsp ghee or olive oil for frying
method: Grate zucchini, toss with salt in a sieve over a bowl. Sit 10 min until moisture releases.
Squeeze and wring out ALL liquid by hand, then scrunch in paper towel — the drier the better.
Whisk eggs in a large bowl. Add zucchini, dill, feta, garlic, lemon zest, flour, and baking powder. Stir to combine.
Heat frying pan over medium heat with 2 Tbsp ghee. Scoop ¼ cup portions, cook 2–3 min each side until golden.
Serve with lemon wedges and yoghurt.
notes: Makes 12 fritters. Keep in fridge 3 days or freeze up to 3 months (omit feta for freezing). Delicious with a fried egg on top. Lunchbox friendly.

title: Mum's Chicken Curry (Sophie)
method: Put ghee and oil into lidded frying pan on medium heat. Add cumin seeds and cinnamon sticks — infuse 1 minute.
Add onions, cook 10–12 minutes until golden brown.
Bash ginger, garlic, and chillies with a pinch of salt into a coarse paste. Add to pan, cook gently 2 minutes.
Pour in passata, stir and cook until thick paste. Add tomato purée, ground cumin, turmeric, and ½ tsp salt.
Whisk yoghurt and add slowly to the curry. Cook until bubbling.
Add chicken, lid on, gentle heat ~30 minutes.
Add ground almonds and garam masala, cook another 5 minutes.
Serve with chapatis, naan, or rice. Extra yoghurt at the table.
notes: Ultimate comfort food. Use boneless thighs for convenience. Ground almonds add body without dairy. Serves 4. ~43g protein per serve (curry only).

title: Chocolate Peanut Energy Balls
method: Blend nuts first until crumbly.
Add remaining ingredients — dates, peanut butter, maple syrup, chocolate, and cacao powder.
Blend until mixture comes together.
Roll into balls.
notes: Simple no-bake energy balls — all organic ingredients. Great snack prep, keeps in fridge or freezer. ~6g protein per ball (batch of ~15). Use any quality sea salt dark chocolate if Pico isn't available.

title: Slow Cooker Rosemary Lamb & Potatoes
ingredients: 1.6kg boneless leg of lamb or shoulder
method: Finely slice onion and place on the base of the slow cooker.
Generously coat the lamb with olive oil, flakey salt, fresh rosemary, and minced garlic.
Add lamb to the slow cooker along with the juice of 1 large lemon.
Cut potatoes into quarters and place on top of the lamb.
No liquid needed — the lamb cooks in its own juices.
Cook on HIGH for larger cuts (>1.6kg), or LOW for smaller cuts. Check for tenderness.
notes: Sarah's Day recipe — dead simple, zero liquid needed. The lamb releases enough juices to cook the potatoes through. Adjust cook time based on size: ~4-5 hours on HIGH, ~8 hours on LOW. ~45g protein per serve.

title: Nourishing Maple Marshmallows
ingredients: 4 Tbsp bovine gelatin (Perfect Supplements — code SASHA10 for 37% off)
method: Bloom the gelatin: pour 1/2 cup water into a bowl, sprinkle 4 Tbsp gelatin on top, let sit a few minutes.
Add 3/4 cup maple syrup, 3/4 cup water, vanilla extract, and pinch of salt to a pot. Heat on medium-low until steamy.
Add bloomed gelatin to the pot and whisk until well combined.
Pour mixture into a stand mixer or large bowl (with hand mixer).
Mix on medium-high for 5-15 minutes until stiff peaks form.
Pour into a baking dish and cool in fridge for minimum 1 hour before cutting.
Add to any warm beverage or eat as a snack.
notes: Homemade marshmallows — no refined sugar, just maple syrup and gelatin. Sasha's code SASHA10 saves 37% on Perfect Supplements bovine gelatin. Great in hot chocolate or coffee.

title: Yogurt Station (Topping Ideas)
ingredients: Any fresh fruit — berries, grated apple, banana
method: Start with a generous bowl of Greek yoghurt.
Set out toppings in small bowls or a compartment tray.
Let everyone build their own bowl.
Great for kids — they love choosing their own toppings.
notes: Not a precise recipe — more of an idea board for yogurt toppings. Great way to use up odds and ends. The purple silicone tray makes it fun for kids. Add a scoop of protein powder or collagen for extra protein.

title: Passionfruit Slice
ingredients: Base: 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup
Filling: 2-3 tbsp honey or maple syrup
Passionfruit pulp for topping (fresh or thawed frozen)
method: Line a slice tin with baking paper.
For the base: place all base ingredients in a food processor and blitz until just combined — don't over-blend. Press evenly into the tin and set aside.
For the filling: blend all filling ingredients (except passionfruit) until completely smooth and creamy.
Pour filling over the base.
Top generously with passionfruit pulp.
Refrigerate until set, then slice and serve.
notes: No-bake, dairy-free, gluten-free. The base is nutty and satisfying. Use preservative-free desiccated coconut for best flavour. Keeps well in the fridge.

title: Coriander & Parsley Herb Dressing
method: Finely chop coriander, parsley, and garlic together.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Combine with olive oil — enough to create a loose, spoonable dressing.
Store in a jar in the fridge.
notes: Jordie makes this weekly — it's her go-to for sprucing up boring meals. Use on salads, scrambled eggs, roasted chicken, roasted potatoes, steak, or anything that needs a fresh herb kick. Keeps well in the fridge.

title: Homemade Organic Granola
method: Preheat oven to 175°C.
In a large mixing bowl, combine oats, nuts, seeds, salt, cinnamon, and shredded coconut. Stir to blend.
Pour in the coconut oil, maple syrup, and vanilla.
Mix well until every oat and nut is lightly coated.
Pour granola onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper and spread evenly.
Bake until golden, ideally 24-38 minutes.
Set a timer every 12-14 minutes to check and stir so it cooks evenly. As it nears done, check every 5 minutes.
Serve with high-protein Greek yoghurt and organic berries.
notes: Jess Emily's recipe, shared by Renee. Simple, classic, delicious. The key is stirring regularly for even golden clusters. Makes a big batch — store in an airtight jar.

title: One-Bowl Choc Chip Collagen Banana Bread
method: Preheat oven to 180°C and line a cake tin.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork.
Add the eggs, melted coconut oil, and maple syrup. Mix until well combined.
Add almond meal, tapioca flour, collagen, baking soda, vanilla, and cinnamon. Stir to combine.
Fold through the chopped chocolate.
Pour into the prepared tin.
Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown and a skewer comes out clean.
Let it cool before slicing, then enjoy.
notes: Jordie's rainy day go-to. Gluten-free, dairy-free, refined sugar-free. One bowl, minimal effort. The collagen adds a protein boost without changing the texture. Use Chief Collagen or similar.

title: Cherry Elderberry Gummies
ingredients: 2 cups cherry juice (or juice of choice)
2 Tbsp Manuka or raw honey (omit for under 12 months)
method: Sprinkle gelatin over the juice in a saucepan and let it bloom for a few minutes.
Gently heat until dissolved — don't boil.
Allow to cool slightly, then stir through the elderberry syrup and honey.
Pour into silicone moulds.
Pop in the fridge to set. That's it.
notes: Suitable from 12 months+ (omit honey for younger babies). A great immune-boosting snack for kids — elderberry + cherry + Manuka honey. Use any juice and any fun moulds.

title: Honey Onion Cough Syrup
ingredients: Good-quality raw honey (enough to cover sliced onions)
Optional: 1 tsp minced ginger or garlic
method: Add finely sliced onion to a saucepan and pour in enough honey to cover. Add any optional extras.
Place on lowest heat for 30 minutes — honey should become warm and runny and smell of onion, but don't let onions overly brown.
Pour mixture into a sterilised glass jar. Seal and store in fridge.
notes: A simple kitchen remedy for soothing coughs and tickly sore throats. Not suitable for children under 12 months. Keeps up to 6 months in the fridge. Offer small amounts off the spoon or mixed into warm tea.

title: Honey Garlic Chicken Mince
ingredients: Sauce: 1/2 cup salt-reduced chicken stock (or water)
method: Heat olive oil in a large frypan on medium-high heat.
Add chicken mince and cook, breaking up with a spoon — approximately 7 minutes until lightly browned.
Meanwhile, make sauce: mix all sauce ingredients except cornflour in a small jug. In a separate bowl, mix cornflour with a few spoons of the sauce until smooth, then add back to the jug.
Add garlic and spring onion to the mince, cook stirring for 1 minute.
Add broccolini, cook 2-3 minutes.
Add sauce, cook stirring while it thickens for a further minute.
Serve in a bowl with rice and shredded coleslaw, in a roll with sriracha, or use as filling for rice paper rolls.
notes: Versatile mince dish — bowl, roll, or rice paper rolls. Sub pork or beef mince. Freezes well, keeps 3 days in fridge. ~35g protein per serve with rice.

title: Yoghurt & Raspberry Muffins
ingredients: 1/2 cup plain full-fat Greek or natural yoghurt
1/4 cup (60ml) melted unsalted butter or extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp vanilla powder or 2 tsp vanilla extract
1 cup raspberries (frozen OK — do not defrost)
method: Preheat oven to 170°C fan-forced. Line a 10-hole muffin tin with cases or use a silicone tin.
In a large mixing bowl, add eggs, yoghurt, butter or oil, honey or maple syrup, and vanilla. Mix until well combined.
Add baking powder, bicarb soda, and salt. Mix briefly until just incorporated.
Add the flour and fold in gently until just combined. Then gently fold in the berries.
Scoop batter between the prepared muffin holes.
Bake 20-30 minutes until golden brown and firm in the centre.
Cool slightly before serving. Store in airtight container in pantry up to 5 days, or freeze up to 3 months.
notes: Lunchbox-friendly, protein-rich muffins. Dairy-free option: use coconut yoghurt. Makes 10. Don't defrost frozen raspberries — add them straight from frozen.

title: Cayenne Lemon Morning Shot
method: Pour lemon juice into a shot glass.
Add olive oil — it forms a middle layer.
Top with cayenne pepper.
Shoot it back. Don't stir.
notes: Morning wellness shot — claimed liver support, circulation, anti-inflammatory, digestive aid. Adjust cayenne to tolerance.

title: Rocky Road
ingredients: 1/2 cup peanut butter or almond butter
2 Tbsp butter (sub extra coconut oil for dairy-free)
method: In a large bowl, add goji berries, sultanas, desiccated coconut, cinnamon, cacao powder, and chopped almonds. Stir well.
Place coconut oil, honey, peanut butter, vanilla, and butter in a small saucepan. Heat over low until melted.
Pour wet mixture into dry ingredients and mix well.
Pour into a baking dish lined with baking paper, smooth with the back of a spoon.
Freeze for 3 hours until set, then cut into pieces. Store in freezer.
notes: Suitable over 2 years. A healthier rocky road — no marshmallows, packed with goji berries, nuts, and coconut. Keeps in the freezer.

title: Yoghurt Bark
ingredients: 2 cups Greek yoghurt (or coconut yoghurt for dairy-free)
Toppings: berries (chopped), activated buckwheat, cacao nibs, hemp seeds, sliced banana, sliced mango, pomegranate seeds, crushed nuts
method: Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Pour yoghurt into the tray and spread until it's a thin even layer.
Drizzle with nut butter (if using).
Sprinkle your chosen toppings all over.
Freeze for a couple of hours until solid.
Break apart into pieces and enjoy. For young babies, let pieces soften slightly before serving.
notes: Suitable 9 months+ depending on toppings. A fun toddler activity — let them help sprinkle toppings. Breaks apart like bark. Store in freezer.

title: Banana Date Protein Smoothie
ingredients: 1/2 cup Greek yoghurt (or coconut for plant-based)
1-2 Tbsp peanut butter or nut butter of choice
1 cup tinned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
Optional: desiccated liver, handful spinach or kale
method: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
Pour into glasses and serve immediately.
notes: High-protein smoothie with chickpeas — sounds odd but you can't taste them. Bonsoy milk adds extra protein. Great for kids. Add spinach for a nutrient boost.

title: Lemon Panna Cotta
ingredients: 2 tsp gelatin (Cell Squared grass-fed — code jordiepieface for 15% off @jivita_lifestyler)
2 Tbsp maple syrup or honey (or to taste)
method: Pour the cream into a saucepan. Place a sieve on top.
Slice lemons lengthwise and scoop out the flesh.
Press the flesh into the sieve to extract the lemon juice.
Add gelatin and sweetener to the cream mix.
Heat on low-medium, simmer a few minutes until gelatin dissolves. Taste and adjust sweetness or lemon.
Pour into ramekins, glasses, or hollowed lemon shells.
Place in fridge until completely set.
notes: Just 4 ingredients. Jordie's tip: serve in the hollowed lemon shells for presentation. Creamy, tangy, simple. Use code jordiepieface at Jivita for 15% off gelatin.

title: Baby-Friendly Lentil Dahl
ingredients: 6 cups bone broth (or water or vegetable stock)
Optional garnishes: avocado, coriander, fresh coconut, chopped tomato, corn kernels, lime, cucumber raita
method: Add all ingredients except coconut milk, tomatoes, lime juice, and garnishes to a large pot.
Bring to boil, then turn down to simmer. Add coconut milk and tomatoes, stir well.
Continue simmering, stirring occasionally, for 30 minutes.
When lentils are soft and consistency is creamy, it's ready. Add more water if you want it thinner.
Remove bay leaves. Add garnishes on top.
Serve with rice, quinoa, or cauliflower rice.
notes: Mildly spiced — perfect flavour introduction for babies. Lentils are a great plant-based source of protein, iron, and fibre. Freezes well. Cucumber raita: Greek yoghurt, mint, cumin, lemon zest and juice.

title: 4-Ingredient Protein Magnums
ingredients: Optional: chocolate chips, 1 frozen banana, liver powder, scoop of collagen
Chocolate coat: 2 blocks Lindt 70% dark chocolate
method: Mix yoghurt, protein powder, peanut butter, and sweetener until smooth. Add any optional extras.
Pour into popsicle moulds, insert sticks.
Freeze until solid.
Melt chocolate in a double boiler or microwave.
Dip frozen bars in melted chocolate, then roll in crushed nuts.
Return to freezer to set the chocolate coat.
notes: ~27g protein per serve. Tastes like a Magnum but made with Greek yoghurt and whey. Use Lindt 70% for the coat. Renee adds liver powder for extra nutrients — optional!

title: Iron-Rich Green Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 cup mixed herbs (parsley, coriander, mint, basil)
method: Add all ingredients to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Serve as a dip, over vegetables, with lamb cutlets, through pasta, or stirred into purées.
notes: Packed with iron from spinach and spirulina, healthy fats from avocado and olive oil. Great for babies and toddlers — a spoonful stirred through meals. From the Milk to Meals series.

title: Ginger Cookies
ingredients: 3 Tbsp white rice flour (or coconut flour)
method: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line two trays with baking paper.
Combine all cookie ingredients together in a bowl evenly.
Roll and press into cookies. If there are any cracked edges, use fingertips to gently smooth the edges.
Bake until golden.
notes: Gluten-free, dairy-free. Simple ginger cookies — the ginger is the star. Drizzle with melted dark chocolate if you're feeling fancy.

title: Hearty Beef & Minestrone with Risoni
ingredients: 500g topside beef, trimmed, cut into small cubes
method: Heat half the oil in a large saucepan on high. Brown beef in 2 batches for 2-3 minutes. Set aside.
Cook sausages in same pan for 2-3 minutes, turning, until browned. Cool, slice thinly, set aside.
Heat remaining oil in same pan on high. Sauté onion and garlic for 2-3 minutes until tender.
Add bacon, celery, carrot, and zucchini. Cook 4-5 minutes until tender.
Return beef and sausages to pan with tomatoes, stock, and water. Bring to boil, reduce heat, simmer uncovered for 30 minutes.
Stir in cannellini beans, shredded cabbage, and risoni. Simmer 8-10 minutes until risoni is tender.
Stir chopped parsley through. Cool.
notes: Freezes well — portion into airtight containers, freeze up to 3 months. Reheat: defrost overnight, bring to boil, simmer 4-5 minutes. Serve with crusty bread.

title: Strawberry Jam Gumnuts
ingredients: 1 Tbsp avocado oil (or oil of choice)
method: Preheat oven to 175°C and line a tray with baking paper.
In a large bowl, combine almond meal, flaxseeds, coconut, baking powder, salt, flour, and ginger. Mix well.
Make a well in the centre, pour in maple syrup and oil. Fold together until a sticky dough forms.
Roll into 11 even balls, place on tray. Press down lightly with thumb to create a dent in each.
Dollop ~1 tsp strawberry jam into each dent.
Bake 15 minutes or until golden.
notes: DF, GF, vegan. Makes 11 cookies. The flaxseeds give them a great speckled texture. Use any jam — raspberry or apricot work well too.

title: 5-Ingredient Honey & Sea Salt Ice Cream
ingredients: Sea salt to sprinkle on top
method: Add all ingredients into a blender and blitz until combined.
Taste and add more honey if desired.
Pour into an ice cream maker and follow its instructions. If you don't have one, pour into a lined container and freeze.
If set solid, allow to thaw 5-10 minutes before scooping.
Drizzle with a little more honey and a pinch of sea salt on top.
notes: No ice cream maker needed. Jordie adds liver powder for nutrients — you can't taste it, but it's optional. Naturally sweetened with honey. The sea salt on top makes it.

title: Cultured Apple-Pie Bircher
ingredients: 2 cups rolled oats (quinoa flakes for GF)
3 cups kefir (or 2 cups Greek yoghurt + 1 cup milk)
method: Add all ingredients to a bowl.
Stir well, cover, and place in the fridge overnight.
Serve cold in the morning. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
notes: Serves 3 adults or 2 adults + 2 kids. Packed with probiotics from kefir, fibre, fat, and protein. No cooking — just stir and leave overnight. A gut-friendly breakfast the whole family can share.

title: Shredded Beef Brisket
ingredients: Spice crust: garlic powder, onion powder, cinnamon, sumac, smoked paprika — whatever you like
method: Preheat oven to 130°C.
In an ovenproof casserole dish over medium heat, brown brisket on both sides. Set aside to rest.
To the hot pan, add garlic and onion, allow to caramelise and soften.
Add diced tomatoes, tomato paste, orange juice, bone broth, maple syrup, and Worcestershire sauce. Return meat to the dish (liquid should come about 2/3 up the meat).
Top meat generously with your chosen spices.
Place lid on and cook in oven for ~6 hours until meat is soft and shreds easily.
Once soft, shred with two forks through the sauce.
Optional: if you want a thicker sauce, turn oven to 180°C, return brisket (lid off) for ~1 hour until caramelised.
notes: Serves 6-8. Freezes well. Serve with mashed veg, in tacos, wraps, with rice, or through pasta — endlessly versatile. The orange juice gives it a subtle sweetness.

title: Thai Basil Chilli Chicken
ingredients: 6 large dried red chillies, roughly chopped
500g (1 lb) chicken thigh fillets, thinly sliced
method: Mix the ingredients for the stir-fry sauce. Set aside for later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Add the garlic, chillies and onion and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken and immediately spread the chicken out in the pan. Allow to sear for almost a minute, then stir-fry. Repeat until the chicken is just cooked.
Add the stir-fry sauce and cook until the sauce is just thickened.
Toss through the bok choy and stir-fry for a minute. Then toss through the basil leaves.
Serve with steamed rice.
notes: Fast, fresh and fabulous stir-fry — ideal for busy weeknights. The key is high heat and not crowding the pan.

title: Osso Buco
ingredients: 1 tbsp ghee or tallow or olive oil
1 sprig rosemary or thyme, finely chopped
Gremolata: zest and 1 tbsp juice of 1 lemon
1 small bunch fresh parsley, finely chopped
method: Oven: Preheat oven to 130°C. In a large casserole dish, heat ghee over medium-high heat and brown the osso buco on both sides. Transfer meat to a bowl.
To the hot pan, add onion, garlic, celery, carrot, herbs and eggplant (if using). Allow to caramelise, stirring occasionally.
Add passata, bone broth, bay leaves and resting juices. Return meat in an even layer — liquid should nearly cover the meat.
Cover and place in the oven for ~6 hours until meat is falling off the bone.
Scoop marrow out of the bones and shred the meat. Season with salt and pepper.
Slow cooker: Brown meat in a frypan, then sauté veg. Transfer everything to slow cooker. Cook on Low 8-10 hours or High 5-6 hours.
Gremolata: Finely chop parsley and garlic, combine with lemon zest, juice and olive oil. Sprinkle over before serving.
Serve with mashed potato/cauliflower, rice, risotto or through pasta.
notes: From the Boob to Food book Toddler to Table. Rich in iron and zinc — ideal for babies starting solids and postpartum mums. Versatile: serve over mash night one, stirred through pasta night two.

title: Slow-Cooked Shredded Chicken
ingredients: Oven: 1 cup chicken broth. Slow cooker: ¼ cup + 2 tbsp
2 tbsp olive oil or cooking fat of choice
Optional: 200g tinned black beans (half a tin, drained)
method: Oven: Preheat oven to 130°C fan-forced.
In a large oven-safe pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion and garlic, sauté until softened.
Remove from heat, deglaze with ½ cup of the broth, scraping up any browned bits.
Add chicken thighs, diced tomatoes, remaining broth, tomato paste, and all spices. Stir well.
Cover and place in oven for 4 hours, until chicken is tender and pulls apart easily.
Shred chicken directly in the pot using two forks. Stir through the sauce.
If using black beans, add now and let residual heat warm them through.

Slow cooker: Sauté onion and garlic in a pan. Add spices and salt, cook 1 min. Deglaze with 2 tbsp broth, brown chicken, add tomatoes and ¼ cup broth. Transfer to slow cooker, cook on Low for 4 hours. Shred and serve.
notes: A nourishing, one-pot family favourite. Works beautifully in a campfire Dutch oven too. Great source of iron, freezer-friendly, and perfect for babies starting solids through to fussy toddlers.

title: Low Carb Choc Chip Cookies
ingredients: 2 cups blanched almond or hazelnut meal (activated if possible)
3 tbsp collagen powder (optional — if omitted, add a touch more almond meal)
⅓-½ cup monk fruit or granulated sweetener of choice
½-1 block dark organic chocolate, chopped
method: Preheat oven to 170°C and line a baking tray.
Add all ingredients into a bowl and stir to combine.
Taste the dough and adjust sweetness if needed.
Roll mixture into balls and place on the lined baking tray.
Press balls as flat as you like — they won't rise much. Keep them fuller for softer, chewier cookies; press flatter for crunchier ones.
Bake for 15 minutes, or until golden brown.
Remove from oven and enjoy warm.
notes: From qualified nutritionist Jordan Pie. Collagen adds a protein, gut-healing and hormonal balancing boost — completely optional. Makes 10-12 cookies.

title: Cashew Cream Chocolate Bars
ingredients: 4 tbsp maple syrup (or more to taste)
1 tsp vanilla powder or 2 tsp vanilla extract
Optional: 2-3 tsp maca powder, 2 tsp ashwagandha or other adaptogens
Choc coating: 1 block quality dark chocolate
¼ cup roasted chopped nuts (almonds, pistachios, cashews, macadamias)
method: Blend all filling ingredients until smooth and creamy.
Pour into moulds (or a lined tin) with wooden sticks inserted. Freeze until firm.
Melt dark chocolate with coconut oil. Stir in chopped nuts.
Dip frozen bars into chocolate coating, letting excess drip off.
Return to freezer to set. Store in freezer, let sit 5 min before eating.
notes: Dairy-free, gluten-free. Adaptogenic add-ins optional — maca and ashwagandha for hormone support. The bone broth adds gut-healing collagen.

title: Gilli's Eight-Hour Lamb
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Preheat oven to 100°C. Cut 8–10 holes into the lamb's skin and fill with garlic cloves and sprigs of rosemary. Season with salt and black pepper.
Place lamb inside oven bag and place into a large roasting dish.
Add onion and tomato to lamb and tie bag according to instructions.
Roast for 8 hours.
To serve, open oven bag at table and serve melt-in-the-mouth lamb with mash and pan juices.
notes: From the Barlow family recipe collection. The oven bag is the secret — it steams the lamb to fall-apart tenderness. Serve with creamy mashed potato to soak up the pan juices.

title: Chicken Coriander Meatballs
method: Combine mince, oyster sauce, garlic, fish sauce, coriander, coconut milk and breadcrumbs in a large bowl.
Shape into 12 patties.
Heat ghee in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook patties for a few minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Serve hot with chilli sauce.
notes: Amy’s version — half the coconut milk, breadcrumbs added, shaped into patties and pan-fried in ghee instead of baked. Makes 12 patties. Serve with sweet chilli sauce for dipping.

title: Fish Fingers
ingredients: 400g white fish (cod, hake, haddock or pollock), skinless, deboned
½ cup flour (plain, spelt, buckwheat or cassava)
method: Preheat oven to 200°C and line a baking tray.
Blitz toasted sourdough in a food processor to fine breadcrumbs. Mix with lemon zest, dill and salt.
Cut fish into finger-sized strips.
Set up dredging stations: flour on one plate, whisked egg in a bowl, breadcrumb mixture on another plate.
Coat each fish strip in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Place on lined tray.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
notes: Makes 12 fish fingers. Freezer-friendly — freeze uncooked on a tray then transfer to a container. Gluten-free option: replace sourdough with gluten-free bread. Serve with Mashed Potato + Cauliflower (page 311), Chips (page 318), Mum's Potato Salad (page 321), or A Simple Side Salad (page 322).

title: Banana Oat Blender Pancakes
ingredients: 2 large or 3 small ripe bananas (1 cup mashed)
2-3 tsp ghee or coconut oil, for frying
method: Add all ingredients into a blender and blend on high until combined and smooth.
Allow the mixture to sit for 10-15 minutes — this helps the batter thicken.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat with a teaspoon of ghee or coconut oil. Scoop batter using 2-3 tbsp per pancake.
Cook until bubbles form on top and edges look dry and set (~2 min). Flip and cook until browned underneath (~2 min). Repeat with remaining batter.
notes: Makes 8-10 small pancakes. High-protein option: sub milk for ½ cup cottage cheese. Keeps in fridge 3 days or freeze up to 3 months. These take longer than traditional pancakes — if burning, lower the heat. Batter can be premade and kept in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Pumpkin Bundt Cake
ingredients: ½ cup (100g) packed brown sugar (halved from original)
⅓ cup (75g) granulated sugar (halved from original)
Optional: 1¼ cups chocolate chips or chopped walnuts/pecans
Optional topping: salted caramel, maple icing, or cream cheese frosting
method: Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C) and grease a 10-12 cup Bundt pan.
Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, and all spices together in a large bowl.
Whisk oil, eggs, brown sugar, granulated sugar, pumpkin, and vanilla until combined. Pour wet into dry and mix until completely combined. Fold in chocolate chips or nuts if using.
Spoon batter into prepared Bundt pan. Bake for 55-70 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean with just a couple moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan on a wire rack for 2 hours, then invert onto a serving plate.
Cool completely before drizzling with topping. Pictured with maple icing and a sprinkle of pumpkin pie spice.
notes: From Meg (work). Sugar already halved in this version — original calls for 1 cup brown + ¾ cup granulated. Amy's note: halve the sugar. Cover tightly and store at room temp for a couple days or fridge up to 5 days.

title: Chocolate Crunch Ice Creams
ingredients: Filling: 2 cups lightly roasted cashews (raw ok)
⅓ cup maple syrup (or ½ cup for sweeter)
2 cups The Monday Food Co Peanut Butter GF Granola (for coating)
method: Optional: Lightly roast cashews in oven for 8-10 minutes until lightly golden for deeper flavour.
Add all filling ingredients to a food processor or Thermomix and blend on high until completely smooth. Scrape down sides and blend again.
Taste and add more maple syrup if you prefer sweeter.
Pour mixture into silicone ice cream moulds and insert sticks. Tap to remove air bubbles, then freeze until set.
For the coating: melt chocolate and coconut oil in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Let chocolate cool slightly, then pour into a cup or jar wide enough for dipping. Add granola to a separate bowl.
Once ice creams are fully frozen, dip each into chocolate, then immediately into granola, pressing gently to stick.
Place on a baking paper-lined tray and repeat. Store in freezer.
notes: Gluten free, dairy free, refined sugar free. Makes 8 ice creams. The Monday Food Co Peanut Butter GF Granola is recommended for the crunch coating.

title: Healthy Girl Scout Tagalong Cookies
ingredients: Filling: ½ cup (129g) peanut butter, chilled
method: Preheat oven to 325°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, mix almond flour, salt, baking soda, maple syrup, olive oil and vanilla until combined. Use hands to bring dough together into a ball.
Place dough between two pieces of parchment paper, press into a flat disc and roll out. Cut out cookies using a small glass (2¼ inch diameter).
Place cookies on baking sheet and bake for 8-10 minutes. Cool on wire rack for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for 1 hour.
Spread about 1 tbsp chilled peanut butter evenly onto each cookie. Place on tray and freeze for at least 1 hour.
Melt chocolate chips with coconut oil in a small pot, stirring constantly until smooth. Transfer to a small bowl.
Coat each cookie in melted chocolate, allowing excess to drip off. Sprinkle with flaky salt. Refrigerate 30 minutes to set.
notes: From Netty. Gluten free and vegan. Makes 14 cookies. All you need is 7 ingredients. Can sub olive oil for coconut oil and honey for maple syrup if needed.

title: Loaded Choccy Muffins
ingredients: 1 cup grated zucchini (squeeze out excess liquid)
⅓ cup oil (avocado, olive or melted coconut)
¼ cup Greek or coconut yoghurt
¼ cup maple syrup or honey
1¼ cups spelt flour or plain flour
¼ cup choc chips (or cacao nibs)
method: Preheat oven to 180°C fan-forced. Line a muffin tin with 10 liners.
In a blender, blend banana, eggs, oil, milk, yoghurt, honey/maple syrup, vanilla, and spinach until smooth.
In a large bowl, mix together flour, cacao powder, baking powder, and cinnamon.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and gently fold to combine.
Add grated zucchini, carrot and choc chips and mix until just combined.
Spoon into muffin liners and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean. Cool before serving.
notes: Makes 10 muffins. Packed with hidden veggies — spinach, zucchini, and carrot. Freezer-friendly. Great lunchbox filler.

title: Easy Mediterranean Chicken Meatballs
ingredients: ¼ cup finely diced red onion
method: Mix all meatball ingredients together in a bowl. Use your hands to ensure everything is well combined.
Divide into desired size and place onto a lined baking tray.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes.
Alternatively, pan-fry until golden and cooked through.
notes: High-protein, meal-prep friendly, gluten-free. Pair with leafy greens, tzatziki or roasted vegetables. Freeze well.

title: Black Bean Brownies
ingredients: 1 can (400g) black beans, rinsed and drained
½ cup honey or maple syrup
¼ cup coconut oil or melted butter
method: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease or line an 8×8-inch baking pan with baking paper.
Add black beans, oats, cocoa powder, honey/maple syrup, coconut oil, eggs, vanilla, baking powder and salt to a food processor or blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out mostly clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Slice into squares.
notes: Makes 12 brownies. Packed with fibre, plant-based protein, folate, magnesium and iron. Store airtight at room temp 2-3 days, fridge up to 1 week, or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Kidney Cleansing Green Juice
ingredients: Other optional: turmeric root, basil, mint
If fermenting: 1 cup coconut water kefir
method: Wash celery, cucumbers and herbs in filtered water.
Chop all veggies and herbs, remove skins from lemons/limes.
Put all ingredients through a juicer and collect the juice.
Drink fresh with ice cubes.
For probiotic version: add juice to a large glass jar, top with coconut water kefir. Close lid and ferment on bench top 4-6 hours. Refrigerate.
notes: Makes roughly 2L. Jordan's go-to for kidney support. Fermenting adds probiotics and preserves nutrients longer.

title: GF Snickers Slice
ingredients: ½ cup melted coconut oil (butter/ghee ok)
Filling: 1 heaped cup smooth peanut butter
method: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a slice tin with baking paper.
Mix all base ingredients together. If too wet, add a few more tbsp almond meal. Press into lined tin evenly.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until dark golden brown. Cool.
For filling: add all ingredients to a small saucepan. Heat on low for ~1 minute until warmed and melted. Mix evenly.
Pour filling over cooled base and refrigerate to set.
Melt chocolate and coconut oil in a saucepan on low heat. Pour over set filling.
Top with chopped roasted peanuts and optional bee pollen/sea salt. Refrigerate until chocolate sets, then slice.
notes: GF, DF, EF, RSF. The filling is quite sweet — Jordan recommends really dark chocolate to balance. Uses coconut condensed milk for an easy no-boil filling.

title: Chicken and Thai Basil Stir-fry with Noodles
ingredients: Sauce: 1 tbsp tamari or soy sauce
1 handful Thai basil or regular basil
method: Make the sauce: combine all sauce ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Prep noodles as per packet instructions. Drain, rinse in cold water, drain again.
Heat olive oil in a large deep frying pan over high heat. Add spring onion, garlic and ginger, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add minced chicken and cook 2-3 minutes until browned, breaking it up as you go.
Add broccolini and sauce, cook 3 minutes until broccolini has softened.
Add basil leaves and stir through.
Serve chicken on vermicelli rice noodles with lime wedges on the side.
notes: From The Simple Dinner Edit cookbook, page 114. Ready in under 20 minutes. Per serve: 504 kcal, 26g protein. Sub broccolini with carrots, sugar snap peas, mushrooms, baby corn or capsicum. Can use pork or beef mince instead. Freezer-friendly.

title: Low Carb Zucchini & Cauliflower Fritters
ingredients: 1 large zucchini, grated (squeeze out excess water)
2 garlic cloves, crushed (or 1 tsp garlic powder)
Coconut oil and ghee, for cooking
method: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Heat a large frying pan on medium heat with 2 tbsp coconut oil/ghee.
Use your hands to shape mixture into fritters and place on hot pan (3-4 at a time). Cook both sides until golden brown.
Transfer to baking tray and keep warm in oven while cooking remaining fritters.
Serve with avocado, poached eggs, roasted tomatoes, or homemade chilli sauce.
notes: ~12g carbs and 9g fibre per fritter. Great low-carb, gluten-free breakfast or lunch. Freezer-friendly.

title: Chicken Tray Bake
ingredients: 2 chorizo sausages or 4 rashers nitrate-free bacon
1 handful cherry tomatoes or sundried tomatoes
1 handful crumbled Danish feta or haloumi
Herbs of choice (basil, rosemary, thyme, oregano)
method: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Place chicken, chorizo, red onion, garlic, lemon, tomatoes and cheese into a large baking tray.
Sprinkle chicken with paprika and salt. If using bacon, lay rashers over the top.
Scatter woody herbs (rosemary/thyme) now; add basil/oregano after cooking.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until chicken is cooked through.
Optional: roast chopped root vegetables on a second tray to serve alongside.
Squeeze roasted lemon over the dish and serve.
notes: One-pan dinner. Dairy-free option: omit cheese. Serve with roasted root vegetables.

title: Immune Boosting Chicken Soup
ingredients: 1 bunch coriander or parsley, finely chopped
2 packets rice noodles or 2 zucchini spiralled
method: Combine garlic, turmeric, ginger, lemon zest, bone broth, chicken and optional broccoli/corn/chilli in a large pot.
Simmer for 10 minutes over low heat until chicken is cooked through.
Cook noodles separately as per packet instructions, drain and add to broth.
Add coconut aminos (if using), lemon juice and coriander/parsley just before serving.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: GF, DF, RSF, EF, NF. Serves 6. Freezes up to 6 months, fridge 3 days. The bone broth base is the key healing component. For babies, puree or cut into safe finger shapes.

title: Wholesome Lamb Ragu
method: Preheat oven 170C. Season lamb.
Sear lamb in olive oil on all sides until golden. Set aside.
Saute garlic and onion. Add carrots, celery, herbs, tomato paste, half tomatoes. Deglaze with wine.
Add stock, cherry tomatoes, bay leaves. Return lamb, cover, oven 4-6hrs. Flip hourly.
Boil pasta. Pull bones from lamb, shred meat. Stir parmesan through.
Serve ragu over pasta with extra parmesan.
notes: Serves 4. From Sarahs Day.

title: 2 Minute Noodles
ingredients: 1 serve noodles (mie goreng, ramen, rice or vermicelli)
1 handful cooked protein — shredded chicken, tofu, beef strips, omelette strips (optional)
method: Heat the bone broth until boiling — either on the stovetop or in the microwave.
Place noodles, frozen veg, and any optional add-ins into a heatproof jar, bowl, or thermos.
Pour the hot broth over everything, cover with a lid or plate, and let sit for 3-4 minutes until noodles are tender.
Give it a stir, season to taste, and enjoy.

title: Best Baked Beans
ingredients: 1 x 400g tin cannellini or butter beans, drained
1 x 400g tin kidney beans (or second tin of white beans)
2 tsp Worcestershire sauce (see notes for vegetarian)
1/2–3/4 cup chicken stock or broth (or more for thinner)
method: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook gently until softened and translucent.
Stir in the garlic and curry powder and cook until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, drained beans, chicken stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, and cracked black pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

title: Oat Crepes
ingredients: 1 tbsp butter or oil for frying
method: Add the oats, milk and vanilla essence to a blender and blend on high until completely smooth.
Add the eggs and pulse until mixed through.
Melt butter in a frying pan on medium heat. Pour about 2-3 tbsp batter and swirl to spread thin.
Cook until small bubbles form, then flip. Repeat for all crepes (makes ~6).
Serve with toppings of choice like chia jam, ricotta or cream cheese.
notes: Amy: add spirulina, protein powder, and/or psyllium husk to boost nutrition.

title: Chicken Bone Broth
ingredients: 500g chicken feet or necks (optional, for gelatin)
Herbs — celery leaves, parsley, thyme, sage, bay leaves
method: Place whole chicken, feet/necks (if using), vegetables, herbs, apple cider vinegar and peppercorns into a large pot.
Fill with water to cover. Bring just to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 2 hours, then remove the chicken. Shred meat for meals, return carcass to pot.
Continue simmering for 12–24 hours, lid on, topping up water as needed.
Strain and cool before storing. Yields ~2L.
notes: Also works in slow cooker (low 12–24hrs) or pressure cooker (high 2hrs). Remove chicken at the 2-hour mark in all methods.

title: Pumped Up Porridge
ingredients: 1 tsp ground flaxseeds, LSA or psyllium husk
Drizzle of coconut or milk kefir (topping)
method: Soaked version: Add oats to a bowl and cover with water. Stir in 1 tsp apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, or whey. Cover and leave in a warm spot for at least 6 hours or overnight. Drain and rinse well.
Quick version: Add oats and milk directly to a small saucepan.
Stir in any optional ingredients like banana, collagen, butter, chia, flaxseeds or egg yolk.
Cook over low heat for 3–5 minutes (soaked) or 5–7 minutes (unsoaked), stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and finish with toppings of choice.

title: Veggie-Bomb Pasta Sauce
ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, ghee, olive oil or coconut oil
3–4 cups chopped root vegetables (sweet potato, pumpkin, swede, parsnip, turnip, beetroot, red capsicum)
Olive oil or ghee for roasting
2 cups bone broth or vegetable stock
2 tbsp raw honey or maple syrup
Optional: bone marrow or up to 250g grated frozen liver (or desiccated liver powder)
method: Preheat oven to 180°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Chop all vegetables: slice onion/leek, fennel, zucchini, mushrooms. Roughly chop carrots, celery and root vegetables. Quarter lemon, leave garlic unpeeled.
Spread root vegetables, carrot, celery, garlic and lemon on trays. Drizzle with ghee or olive oil and roast ~45 minutes until soft and browned.
Meanwhile, sauté onion/leek, fennel, mushrooms and zucchini in butter/ghee/oil until browned and softened.
Transfer roasted veg + sautéed veg to a large pot. Squeeze in garlic and lemon (discard skins). Add broth, passata, tomatoes, basil, spinach, balsamic and honey.
If using grated liver or bone marrow, stir in now.
Simmer gently, season with salt and pepper.
Blend with stick blender or in batches until smooth.
Portion into jars for storage.
notes: Hidden-veggie powerhouse — 10–12 serves. Freezes well in portions.

title: ANZAC Biscuits
method: Preheat oven to 160°C fan-forced and line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine all ingredients and stir until well mixed.
Use a tablespoon to scoop the mixture, roll into balls, and place evenly on the tray.
Gently flatten each ball with your fingertips.
Bake for 20 minutes, or until golden. Allow to cool before serving.
notes: Healthier twist on traditional ANZACs — maple syrup instead of golden syrup. Optional collagen for extra protein. Makes 20 biscuits. Store in airtight container in fridge up to 5 days, freeze up to 3 months.

title: Slow-Cooker Chicken, Bacon & Leek Pie
method: If your slow cooker has a Sauté function, use it now. Otherwise use a frying pan.
Cook the bacon until lightly golden.
Add the leek and cook for 5–7 minutes until softened. Stir through the garlic, thyme leaves and smoked paprika and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with a splash of the bone broth, scraping up any browned bits from the base.
Add the remaining broth, chicken thighs and bay leaves. The liquid should come roughly halfway up the chicken, not completely cover it.
Cook on Low for 6 hours or High for 3–4 hours.
Remove and discard the bay leaves, then shred the chicken directly into the sauce using two forks.
Stir through the Dijon mustard, frozen peas and crème fraîche.
If the filling isn't thick enough, whisk together the flour and water to make a slurry. Stir into the slow cooker and cook on Reduce/High for 15 minutes to thicken.
Taste and season with salt as needed.
Divide the filling between individual pie dishes or spoon into one large pie dish.
Top with puff pastry, trim edges, brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes, or until the pastry is puffed and golden brown.
notes: Adapted from Toddler to Table cookbook. Filling can be made days in advance or frozen up to 3 months. Thaw, top with fresh puff pastry and bake.

title: Choc Banana Popsicles
method: Prepare a baking tray with baking paper.
Use the double boiler method to melt vegan choc chips, then remove from the heat.
Peel bananas and cut each in half. Slide the base of each banana onto a popsicle stick.
Pour buckwheat groats onto a plate and have your crunchy peanut butter ready.
Coat each banana pop in a layer of crunchy peanut butter.

Once thoroughly covered in peanut butter, roll it around on the plate of buckwheat groats (or crunchy ingredient of choice). Don't be afraid to use your hands and lightly press the buckwheat groats into the peanut butter so it sticks properly!
Dip/roll the peanut butter and buckwheat groat-covered banana in the melted chocolate. Use a spoon or rubber spatula to help drizzle chocolate all over the banana until evenly coated.
Place coated bananas onto the baking tray and place in the freezer to set for at least 3 hours.
Remove from the freezer and allow to sit at room temperature for 5-10 minutes before eating!
Feel free to play around with this recipe and create your own favourite combinations. Also love sultanas, coconut and maple syrup underneath the chocolate!
notes: DF, GF, V, VG. Makes 8 pops. Make sure to remove chocolate from the heat just before it's completely melted — continue to stir until smooth.

title: Quick Dill & Chicken Meatballs
ingredients: 2 heaped Tbsp fresh dill, finely chopped
method: Preheat oven to 175°C and prepare a large tray with baking paper.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl and mash together using a fork (or combine in a food processor).
Using a small ice cream scooper, scoop out 12 even balls and place onto your prepared baking tray.
Bake in the oven for 17 minutes (flip each meatball at the 10 minute mark) or until lightly golden.
Serve with your favourite side or store in an airtight container in the fridge and use for meal preps or nourish bowls on demand.
notes: DF, GF, NF. Makes 12 meatballs. Mixture will be sticky so don't use your hands — use a spoon or ice cream scooper instead. Don't leave them in the oven too long as they will dry out!

title: Amy's Mashed Potato
ingredients: 1 can (400g) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 tsp Cell Squared organ meats powder
Optional: carrot, pumpkin, or cauliflower (steamed with the rest)
method: Steam all the vegetables (potatoes, sweet potato, and any optional extras) until tender.
Transfer the steamed vegetables to a Thermomix (or food processor) and blitz until smooth.
Add the butter, drained cannellini beans, and organ meats powder, then blitz again until creamy.
Season to taste and serve.
notes: Serves 6. Optional extras: add carrot, pumpkin, or cauliflower — steamed with the other veg. All vegetables are steamed, then blitzed in the Thermomix; the butter, cannellini beans and organ meat powder go in once the veg is in the Thermomix. Great with slow-cooked lamb.

title: Easy Lemon Cake
ingredients: ½ cup (125 ml) melted unsalted butter, ghee or coconut oil
½ cup (125 ml) lemon juice (about 2–4 lemons)
method: Preheat the oven to 170°C fan-forced. Grease and line a 20 cm cake tin.
Add all ingredients to a food processor and blend until smooth and combined into a batter. Pour into the prepared tin.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Turn the oven off, but leave the cake in the oven for another 5 minutes with the door slightly ajar. Remove and cool completely in the tin.
Drizzle with white chocolate and sprinkle with lemon zest (if using). Slice and enjoy at room temperature or warmed, with homemade custard, vanilla ice cream or yoghurt.
notes: Optional topping: 250 g white chocolate + zest of 1 lemon. Keeps in the fridge up to 3 days, or freeze up to 3 months (freezing changes the texture). Refrigerated is like a crumbly lemon mud cake. Quick and easy with minimal washing up — little ones can help put all the ingredients in the food processor.
